paras: The Lauderdale County whitecapping of 1903 was a series of attacks by a band of 'whitecaps' on Black tenants in Lauderdale County, Tennessee, in January 1903, in which shots were fired into a cabin, a horse was killed and Black families were ordered to leave. No one was reported hurt, but residents petitioned the governor and a mass meeting at Ripley authorized a $200 reward for the capture of those responsible.

The attacks centered on the Maclin High Ground section of Lauderdale County, in the river districts, on the farm of Capt. W. H. Foster near Ripley, where Black families lived as tenants. The Bolivar Bulletin said the depredations were 'a matter of much concern to some of the property owners' of the section.

In the latter part of January 1903, according to the Bolivar Bulletin, the band shot into a Black family's cabin on the Foster plantation, throwing the occupants into a panic. In the same shooting a horse belonging to a Black tenant was killed. The Comet reported that the whitecaps 'ordered several families of negroes on the place to leave the country', and the Bulletin said notices had been placed on many Black houses warning the occupants to leave 'or suffer the consequences'. The same gang was also charged with burning timber intended for building.

A petition asking the governor to offer a reward for the capture and conviction of the whitecappers was circulated in Ripley and was widely signed. In early or mid-February a mass meeting of citizens of Ripley and Lauderdale County at the courthouse raised a subscription and authorized the chairman of the County Court to offer a $200 reward. No report of arrests, a trial or payment of the reward appears in the coverage.

Coverage was confined to Tennessee weeklies: the Johnson City Comet ran a one-paragraph item on January 29 under 'State News in Brief', and the Bolivar Bulletin printed a fuller account the next day and a report on the reward on February 20. The Bulletin condemned the band as 'law-breakers' and 'miscreants' engaged in 'nefarious work' who were 'terrorizing the colored population', while the Comet's brief, without comment of its own, described the petition as seeking the governor's aid against 'this kind of lawlessness'. Neither paper named any of the Black tenants, and no Black newspaper coverage of the episode was found.

reader.title: Lauderdale County whitecapping of 1903
bases: A band the papers call 'whitecaps' or 'whitecappers' shot into a Black tenant's cabin, killed a horse and posted notices ordering Black families to leave (A2, A3, A4).

Two Tennessee papers in different wording (The Comet, A2; the Bolivar Bulletin, A3) report the attack on the Foster place, and the Bulletin's later report of the mass meeting (A4) confirms the whitecapping.

accounts.label: Report of the Ripley mass meeting
accounts.gist: Citizens met at the courthouse, raised money and authorized a $200 reward to stop whitecappers who had been shooting into Black tenant houses.

framing.detail: The Bolivar Bulletin called the whitecappers 'law-breakers' and 'miscreants' doing 'nefarious work', noting the matter concerned 'property owners'.
